newsitem.title: SWEDEN: TENNIS-SWEDEN WINS DOUBLES TO LEAD IN DAVIS CUP TIE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SWEDEN WINS DOUBLES TO LEAD IN DAVIS CUP TIE.

text.p: Sweden took a 2-1 lead over South Africa in their Davis Cup world group quarter-final by winning a five-set doubles clash on Saturday.
Jonas Bjorkman and Nicklas Kulti beat David Adams and Ellis Ferreira 7-5 2-6 6-4 6-7 (6-8) 6-2 after missing two match points in the fourth set.
"It was a tough match but it doesn't really matter if you win in the third or fifth set," Bjorkman said.
Adams said he and Ferreira had played well, especially at the net. "But the one thing we could have done a bit better was to serve a bit better," he said.
The tie will be decided in Sunday's reverse singles with the first match looking crucial, bringing together the teams' respective number ones, Thomas Enqvist and Wayne Ferreira, no relation to Ellis.
Enqvist, 23, ranked seventh in the world, and Ferreira, 25, ranked 10th, have met twice before and the 25-year-old South African, nicknamed "Swede killer" by local media, leads 2-0.
South African captain Danie Visser was confident his team could still secure the semi-final slot against Spain or Italy.
"It is still in my opinion 50-50," Visser said. "I think we have a good shot at winning both matches tomorrow."
The final match will have Bjorkman facing Grant Stafford, who lost to Enqvist 7-5 2-6 6-4 6-1 on Friday.
Wayne Ferreira had levelled the tie 1-1 beating Bjorkman 6-3 6-4 2-6 7-6 (7-3).
Bjorkman, playing before his home town crowd in the southern Swedish town of Vaxjo, is in both singles and doubles because Magnus Larsson withdrew with a foot injury.

The doubles began with two service breaks, then a double fault by Ferreira in the 11th game gave the decisive break to the Swedes, who were cheered on from the sidelines by now-retired Davis Cup stalwart Stefan Edberg.
Ferreira and Adams, ranked 10th and 27th in world doubles respectively, did not give the Swedes a chance in the second set, breaking Kulti's serve in the sixth and Bjorkman in the eighth.
In the third set both pairs held serve until the Swedes broke Adams for a 5-4 lead.
But the South Africans were not done and they broke Bjorkman's serve in the sixth game of the fourth set. The Swedes immediately broke back against Adams and the set went to a tie-breaker.
The tourists took it 8-6 after the Swedes missed two match points, one on Bjorkman's serve.
Sweden swept through the final set with breaks in the sixth and eighth game, Adams double faulting on the final point.
